videos.headline: Green to Anderson, out Bowled!! Full, quick, past the forward pushing outside-edge, and boom, timber. You knew it was coming, and it now officially has. The urn, the Ashes, will remain in Australia, and they've needed just twelve days to get the job done. Anderson b Green 2(4)

Boland to Robinson, out Caught by Labuschagne!! Australia are one wicket away from retaining the Ashes! Boland's on fire, taking down England singlehandedly. Haven't seen a spell as impressive as this one by Boland. That's a length delivery on off, skids along the deck and shapes away slightly. Robinson has a poke and gets an outside edge that flies straight to Labuschagne at third slip. No stopping the Victorian! Robinson c Labuschagne b Boland 0(2)

Boland to Mark Wood, out Caught&Bowled!! A five-wicket haul on debut for Scott Boland! His team mates charge towards him and give him a hug and congratulate him. What a proud moment for the Victorian. Pitches this up around middle and off, and Wood chips it straight back at him. Sharp reflexes as he takes it in his followthrough and England are sinking. Two wickets away from losing the series. The crowd is absolutely loving this. Mark Wood c and b Boland 0(3)

Boland to Root, out Caught by Warner!! That's it, there's the Ashes gone for England - Root falls and there's that last blow for England - Boland is simply on a roll, what a magical debut he's having, in front of his home crowd at the 'G'. Kept to full and kept it simple, a hint of swing away from the right-hander and Root is drawn into a wafty push, plays away from his body, plays with hard hands and the edge settles nicely into the hands of Warner at first slip. He's chuffed to bits, so is Boland and so is entire Australia. Can England save an innings defeat? The players will take drinks at the fall of Root. Root c Warner b Boland 28(59) [4s-4]

Boland to Bairstow, out Lbw!! Bairstow has been given OUT LBW. Paul Wilson thought long and hard before raising the finger, Bairstow has reviewed it though - no bat for sure, but is the impact outside the line of off-stump? Bairstow was turned inside out by the angle, RTS confirms no bat - it's umpire's call on both counts, Bairstow can consider himself terrribly unlucky, but he's OUT. Boland is on a roll, angled in and then nipped away ever so slightly to open up Bairstow completely - turned into an 'S', beaten on the outside edge and rapped on the back-pad, the impact was marginal, just around off and was going on to clip the off-stump. England don't lose their review, but lose Bairstow and their sixth wicket, with still 22 runs in the deficit. Bairstow lbw b Boland 5(18)

Starc to Stokes, out Bowled!! Right through Stokes's defences and Starc has struck early, with England still in the arrears. On a length and a hint of nip back into the left-hander, but poor from Stokes as he left a yawning gap between bat and pad - was pressing forward on the defensive push and is beaten on the inside edge, the ball goes on and hits the top of middle and leg. He looked positive this morning, but England slump further with Root left stranded at the other end. Stokes b Starc 11(16) [4s-2]

Mark Wood to Labuschagne, out Caught by Root!! The jumpy Labuschagne gets squared up, and the jumpy Labuschagne falls. This is what raw pace does -- hurry people up on the back foot, with the ball kicking up off a length, taking the splice in his defence to first slip at a nice comfortable height. And just like that, England have a big foot in the door. Labuschagne c Root b Mark Wood 1(14)

Robinson to Lyon, out Caught by Buttler!! The first real proper fuller length delivery in the channel that England have bowled all morning, and Lyon goes driving straight up. But the ball straightens off the deck, takes a thick outside-edge, and Buttler doesn't mess up. Lyon c Buttler b Robinson 10(22) [4s-2]

Anderson to Warner, out Caught by Crawley!! There comes the poke, there comes the nick, and out of nowhere, in the dying moments of the day, Anderson returns to redeem whatever little confidence there remains for England in this Test. It's a pretty trademark line -- short of a good length, just outside off, angling across. Warner hangs his bat out tentatively, getting squared up too as he tries dabbing it towards third man, but only finds the outside-edge dipping low to gully, where Crawley does well to dive in front, in time. Warner c Crawley b Anderson 38(42) [4s-5]

Cummins to Malan, out Caught by Warner!! Edged and this time it has carried nicely through to Warner at first slip - that's a body blow for England, right at the stroke of lunch on Boxing day. Malan walks off disconsolate and is followed by his partner. Three wickets in the session and all three to the mighty impressive Cummins - pitched up in that channel around off and it just straightened enough to catch Malan's edge, even as he prodded forward. It carried nicely through to Warner who doesn't drop those. England find themselves in trouble once again, this time at the 'G'. Malan c Warner b Cummins 14(66) [4s-1]

Cummins to Crawley, out Caught by Green!! Both the English openers are back to the pavilion, and Cummins has got both of them! The start keeps getting better and better for Australia. Short of a length around off, decks away to an extent and Crawley who looks to defend it off the back foot, gets surprised due to the carry. A thick outside edge is induced due to the pace and bounce, and it flies to gully where Green completes a good low catch. Cummins making the most of the new cherry, the skipper's leading from the front. Crawley c Green b Cummins 12(25)

Cummins to Crawley, out Caught by Green!! Both the English openers are back to the pavilion, and Cummins has got both of them! The start keeps getting better and better for Australia. Short of a length around off, decks away to an extent and Crawley who looks to defend it off the back foot, gets surprised due to the carry. A thick outside edge is induced due to the pace and bounce, and it flies to gully where Green completes a good low catch. Cummins making the most of the new cherry, the skipper's leading from the front. Crawley c Green b Cummins 12(25)

Cummins to Haseeb Hameed, out Caught by Carey!! Haseeb Hameed's gone for a duck! That's edged and taken. Cummins is back to lead Australia and he strikes in his first over and the crowd at the G goes berserk. A perfect length delivery outside off by the Australian captain and it shapes away ever so slightly. Haseeb Hameed tries to defend it and gets a nick. Carey completes the formalities and England are one wicket down. A perfect start for the Aussies, having elected to bowl first. Haseeb Hameed c Carey b Cummins 0(10)
